themes: US AI infrastructure names (MSTR, ORCL, CRWD) are decoupling from Indonesian tech, driven by dollar liquidity and enterprise AI spend, not local fundamentals.

Global risk-on signal (WATCH) favors high-beta US software/semiconductors over IDX tech, which lacks equivalent liquidity and earnings revision momentum.
sectors.ai: Buy selective US-listed AI/infrastructure names (MSTR, PLTR, ORCL) on momentum, but keep Indonesia tech exposure minimal—local names lag US beta and lack earnings catalysts. Rotate any ID tech overweight into US proxies or cash; watch for pullback in MSTR/PLTR to add.

themes: Indonesia's downstream processing mandate continues to structurally re-rate mining equities, favoring smelters and integrated producers over raw ore exporters.
Global tin supply deficits, driven by Myanmar disruptions and rising electronics demand, provide durable upside for TINS and ITMA beyond near-term volatility.
Energy cost divergence—cheaper domestic coal and gas versus elevated US prices—creates persistent margin advantages for Indonesian miners, reinforcing the ID/US performance gap.

Rotate out of US-exposed laggards as ID outperformance persists. Position for Q3 earnings beats in smelters, hedge with DWGL for energy cost tailwinds.

sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: US rate-cut expectations structurally favor long-duration renewable assets and utility capex cycles, compressing discount rates on FSLR/ENPH-style cash flows.
Indonesia's energy transition hinges on JETP-linked grid upgrades and captive industrial solar PPAs, rewarding developers with bankable off-takers (PCG, MPOW) over speculative capacity.
Climate-tech bifurcation persists: US policy-driven demand (IRA credits) outpaces Indonesia's regulatory lag, making US-listed names the safer beta for regional capital.
sectors.ai: Buy pullbacks in US-listed renewables (FSLR, ENPH) and defensive utilities (EIX, PPL) on rate-cut tailwinds; Indonesia underperformed (-0.59%) but PCG/MPOW strength signals selective domestic appetite—rotate into names with contracted PPAs and grid-expansion exposure. Trim pure-play Indonesian developers lacking financing clarity; favor US yield-sensitive equipment makers into Q4.

sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
themes: Small/mid-cap consumer names are driving sector gains, reflecting a structural shift toward domestic discretionary spending as urban incomes rise faster than inflation.
Digital-first FMCG distribution channels are enabling rapid brand scaling for new entrants, compressing time-to-market and disrupting traditional incumbents' shelf-space moats.
The persistent ID-vs-US spread indicates local currency stability and improving purchasing power, underpinning a durable consumption upgrade cycle in tier-2/3 cities.
sectors.ai: Buy selective momentum in small/mid-cap consumer names (KKES, TOOL, WMPP) while large-cap FMCG lags; the ID outperformance vs US signals domestic demand resilience. Rotate into high-beta winners with volume confirmation, but trim any holding that breaks its 5-day average. Focus on names with earnings catalysts or new product launches within 30 days to capture follow-through.
